# AWS Cloud WAN Blueprints

> Guidance and deployable patterns for AWS Cloud WAN. `policy/` documents what a core network policy can express, capability by capability; `infra/` ships CloudFormation and Terraform patterns that deploy a working core network to test a policy on.

The two trees are deliberately decoupled, and understanding the split is most of what you need to navigate this repository. An `infra/` pattern is defined **only** by which attachment types it creates — it does not encode a use case. So **a use case is a policy, not a directory**: do not look for a directory matching a requirement. Compose the policy from the `policy/` pages, then pick the pattern that creates the attachment types the policy needs.

`policy/` ships **composable snippets only** — a fragment of one array, inline next to the prose explaining it. It contains no complete, deployable policy documents. The only full policies in this repository are the `infra/<pattern>/baseline*.json` files, which exist to make a pattern deploy a working network rather than to demonstrate a capability.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): What these blueprints are, the three-layer structure, how to consume them, Cloud WAN fundamentals vocabulary, prerequisites, and the FAQ. Answers "what is in this repository and how do I use it?"
- [SKILLS.md](SKILLS.md): Written for an AI agent. Cloud WAN knowledge (what it is, the policy model, constraints that bite, when to use it over Transit Gateway or VPC Lattice) plus a generator workflow that turns a stated requirement into a validated policy document. Answers "how do I reason about Cloud WAN, and how do I build a policy from requirements?"
- [CONVENTIONS.md](CONVENTIONS.md): The contract every pattern follows — naming, directory layout, version pins, license headers, policy authoring rules, CloudFormation/Terraform parity, and the CI checks. Answers "how must a contribution to this repository be shaped?"
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): How to open an issue or pull request, and the local tool versions that reproduce CI.

## Network policy guidance

One page per top-level area of the policy document. Read the page for an array before writing that array; the pages carry the real field names and constraints.

- [policy/README.md](policy/README.md): Index of the capability pages, the page-to-JSON-array mapping, why the repository ships snippets rather than example policies, and how to validate a policy with the change-set workflow. Answers "which page covers the part of the document I need?"
- [policy/1-core_network_version_configuration.md](policy/1-core_network_version_configuration.md): Produces `version` and `core-network-configuration`. Which policy version to declare and what `2025.11` unlocks over `2021.12`, choosing and pinning ASN ranges, declaring edge locations, inside CIDR blocks for Connect attachments, and the `vpn-ecmp-support`, `dns-support` and `security-group-referencing-support` switches. Answers "which Regions and BGP identities does my core network have, and which decisions here cannot be walked back?"
- [policy/2-segments-and-nfg.md](policy/2-segments-and-nfg.md): Produces `segments` and `network-function-groups`. Segments as global routing domains, `isolate-attachments`, scoping a segment to a subset of Regions, `require-attachment-acceptance`, the `deny-filter` and `allow-filter` guardrails, and which axis to segment on. Answers "what are my routing domains, and how many should there be?"
- [policy/3-attachment_policies.md](policy/3-attachment_policies.md): Produces `attachment-policies`. How an attachment lands in a segment or a network function group, all the match condition types, rule ordering and first-match-wins, `tag` versus `constant` association, and who controls the tags in a shared core network. Answers "how do attachments join the right segment automatically?"
- [policy/4-segment_sharing.md](policy/4-segment_sharing.md): Produces `segment-actions` with `action: share`. Sharing is bidirectional and non-transitive, the three `share-with` forms including the wildcard, and how a routing policy's direction is read from the segment named in `segment`. Answers "how do two routing domains reach each other, and why does sharing not chain?"
- [policy/5-service_insertion.md](policy/5-service_insertion.md): Produces `network-function-groups` and `segment-actions` with `send-to` or `send-via`. Egress versus east-west inspection, `single-hop` versus `dual-hop`, `when-sent-to`, `with-edge-overrides`, appliance mode, the route tables each action builds, and the constraints on mixing modes. Answers "how do I put a firewall in the path, and where does inspection happen?"
- [policy/6-static_routes.md](policy/6-static_routes.md): Produces `segment-actions` with `action: create-route`. Writing an explicit route or a blackhole into one segment, why a static route never crosses a share, and the two-pass deployment that naming attachment IDs forces. Answers "how do I state a route outright, and why should I avoid it?"
- [policy/7-routing_policies.md](policy/7-routing_policies.md): Produces `routing-policies`. Route filtering, summarization and BGP attribute modification; the match conditions and the full action table; which actions are terminal and the rule ordering that follows from it; the three association scopes; summarizing toward on-premises; preferring one Region's hybrid edge with AS_PATH prepending; filtering by BGP community; and the constraints, including that routing policies do not apply to a network function group. Answers "how do I filter, summarize, or steer routes with BGP attributes?"
- [policy/8-edge_location_associations.md](policy/8-edge_location_associations.md): Produces `segment-actions` with `action: associate-routing-policy`. Applying routing policies to one segment's routes crossing one Core Network Edge pair, and reading direction from the first-named edge. Answers "how do I control inter-Region propagation for one Region pair?"
- [policy/9-attachment_routing_policy_rules.md](policy/9-attachment_routing_policy_rules.md): Produces `attachment-routing-policy-rules`. Binding routing policies to attachments through a routing-policy label, what `inbound` and `outbound` mean at attachment scope, scoping a rule to specific Regions, and the cross-account ordering problem when the attachment owner cannot set its own label. Answers "how do I apply a routing policy to a specific attachment?"

## Deployable infrastructure patterns

A pattern is a set of attachment types plus a working baseline policy. Every pattern ships both CloudFormation and Terraform, declares `us-east-1` and `eu-west-1` as edge locations, and forwards traffic on deploy without you writing anything.

- [infra/README.md](infra/README.md): The pattern catalog and how to choose, prerequisites per pattern, how to point a pattern at a policy of your own, what to change to use different Regions, and the attachment association contract shared by the patterns. Answers "which pattern do I deploy, and what do I change to fit my environment?"
- [infra/1-basic/README.md](infra/1-basic/README.md): Creates `vpc` attachments. Three spoke VPCs per Region across two Regions; the baseline demonstrates tag-based association, global segments, non-transitive sharing to an isolated `shared` segment, and the resulting reachability table. Answers "how does a VPC connect to a core network, and what does segmentation actually block?"
- [infra/2-inspection/README.md](infra/2-inspection/README.md): Creates `vpc` attachments for spokes and inspection VPCs, plus AWS Network Firewall and NAT gateways. The baseline demonstrates `send-to` egress inspection on both segments and `send-via` `single-hop` east-west inspection with an edge override, and how to tell which firewall inspected a flow. The most expensive pattern. Answers "how do I deploy and verify traffic inspection with service insertion?"
- [infra/3-transit_gateway/README.md](infra/3-transit_gateway/README.md): Creates `transit-gateway-route-table` attachments. A Transit Gateway per Region peered with the core network, with route tables bound to segments — the coexistence and migration path. Answers "how does an existing Transit Gateway connect to Cloud WAN?"
- [infra/4-hybrid/README.md](infra/4-hybrid/README.md): Creates `vpc`, and optionally `site-to-site-vpn` and `direct-connect-gateway` attachments. The one pattern that applies no attachment tags — it associates by attachment type with a constant segment. Builds the AWS side only. Answers "how does on-premises connectivity attach, and when should association match on type instead of a tag?"
- [infra/5-multi_account/README.md](infra/5-multi_account/README.md): Creates no attachments; spoke accounts create their own. Sharing a core network through AWS RAM, which attachment types a spoke account may create and which it may not, why the share is made from `us-east-1` while the core network is managed from `us-west-2`, and using `require-attachment-acceptance` when a spoke account sets the tag that picks the segment. Answers "how do other accounts attach to my core network, and how do I govern that?"
- [infra/6-prefix_list_association/README.md](infra/6-prefix_list_association/README.md): Creates no attachments. Associating a managed prefix list so a routing policy can match on its alias, the circular dependency that makes a core network's first policy unable to name an alias, the two-document deployment that resolves it, and the mirror-image problem on teardown. Answers "how do I use a managed prefix list in a routing policy?"
- [infra/tf_modules/](infra/tf_modules/): The shared Terraform modules the patterns call — `compute` for test instances and endpoints, `firewall_policy` for the Network Firewall example policy. Terraform only; CloudFormation templates are self-contained.

## Where the complete policies are

- `infra/<pattern>/baseline.json`: The working policy each pattern deploys with. These are the only complete, deployable policy documents in the repository.
- `infra/<pattern>/baseline_<stage>.json`: A later stage, where a service dependency requires policies to be applied in more than one pass. Only [`infra/6-prefix_list_association/`](infra/6-prefix_list_association/README.md) needs one today.
- `infra/<pattern>/cloudformation/core_network*.yaml`: **Generated** from the suffix-paired `baseline*.json`. Never hand-edit these; regenerate with `.github/scripts/check_policies.py`, which CI also uses to fail a template that has drifted from its JSON document.

## Common questions and where they are answered

- **"Should we use Cloud WAN, or Transit Gateway?"** → [SKILLS.md](SKILLS.md), *When to use Cloud WAN*. The recommendation splits on whether the network already exists.
- **"How do I stop two environments talking to each other?"** → You do not: there is no deny action. Segments are unreachable until shared, so the answer is the absence of a `share`. See [policy/4-segment_sharing.md](policy/4-segment_sharing.md).
- **"My attachment is `AVAILABLE` but has no segment."** → The tags the infrastructure applies and the conditions the policy matches disagree, or the attachment is in a Region the policy does not declare. The quietest failure in Cloud WAN. See [policy/3-attachment_policies.md](policy/3-attachment_policies.md) and the association contract in [infra/README.md](infra/README.md).
- **"My policy deployed cleanly and advertises nothing."** → A catch-all `drop` removed what a non-terminal action produced. Non-terminal actions need their own `allow` above the `drop`. See [policy/7-routing_policies.md](policy/7-routing_policies.md).
- **"Traffic is not reaching the firewall, and nothing reports an error."** → For inspection between attachments of the same segment, the segment must be isolated; without it the direct route wins. See [policy/5-service_insertion.md](policy/5-service_insertion.md) and [policy/2-segments-and-nfg.md](policy/2-segments-and-nfg.md).
- **"My route filter looks like it did not work."** → `list-core-network-routing-information` shows state *before* routing policies are applied. Verify with `get-network-routes`. See [policy/7-routing_policies.md](policy/7-routing_policies.md).
- **"Our IP ranges overlap."** → Cloud WAN is IP routing and addresses must be unique. Overlapping CIDRs need Amazon VPC Lattice or AWS PrivateLink instead. See [SKILLS.md](SKILLS.md).
- **"How do I check a policy before it changes anything?"** → Create a policy version and review the change set Cloud WAN generates before executing it. That is the authoritative, state-aware validation, and no offline check substitutes for it. See [policy/README.md](policy/README.md).
